# When to register

Do the [OSF Preregistration](https://osf.io/registries) when the
specification YAML is final and the shared skeletons exist. s0 built the plan,
you generated the Excel specification from it, and no stage after s0 has run.

Every answer of the form then comes from two files. These are the
specification YAML, `spec_vNNN.yaml`, and the Excel specification,
`spec_vNNN.xlsx`. After s0 the Excel specification holds two sheets, "Study
Specification" and "Target trial protocol". The protocol sheet documents one
ETT, the first of the grid unless `protocol_ett_id` names another. Once s1 has
run, a "Rare conditions" sheet follows the Study Specification sheet when
the spec has a `rare_condition_rule`. This article maps each OSF section to a YAML key
and to a section of the Study Specification sheet.

# Produce the Excel specification

`$excel_spec_summary()` writes the Excel specification from the plan that s0
builds. Run `tteplan_check_spec()` on the YAML first. It reads the YAML and no
data.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
swereg::tteplan_check_spec("/path/to/spec/spec_v001.yaml")

study <- swereg::registrystudy_load("/path/to/meta")
plan <- swereg::tteplan_from_spec_and_registrystudy(
  study = study,
  candidate_dir_spec = "/path/to/spec",
  candidate_dir_tteplan = "/path/to/plans/my_study",
  candidate_dir_results = "/path/to/results",
  spec_version = "v001"
)
plan$excel_spec_summary()
plan$print_target_checklist()
```

s0 reads the specification YAML and the registry codes of the
`RegistryStudy`. It also loads the first skeleton batch to validate the
specification:

- It checks that each named column exists. It reads the outcome columns by
  name only, and reads no outcome value.
- It reads the values of the treatment, washout and categorical confounder
  columns, and the type of the observation column.
- It takes the last week of the data as the administrative end.

A failed check stops s0 or gives a warning. A message can state a count of
prevalent-user weeks, or a category value that the data hold and the
specification lacks. You MAY pass `global_max_isoyearweek` to set the administrative end
yourself, and s0 then skips this validation.

`tteplan_excel_spec_summary()` writes the Excel specification from the
specification YAML and a code registry, without a plan. It reads no skeleton,
so it runs before s0, and while the skeletons do not yet hold a new code. Pass
the `RegistryStudy`, or its `$summary_table()`, as `code_registry`, and each
variable that the registry generates shows its codes. The `Admin censoring:` row reads
`not built (spec only)` unless you pass `global_max_isoyearweek`. Every other
cell matches `$excel_spec_summary()` at s0 for the same spec, code registry,
`period_width` and `protocol_ett_id`. Do not edit the workbook by hand:
change the YAML and write the workbook again.

Register after s0 and before s1.

# Write the OSF text

`tteplan_osf_text()` writes the text of each OSF field that the specification determines, from the specification YAML and the code registry. It reads no skeleton, so it runs before s0. It returns a named character vector of Markdown texts, one for each field:

```r
osf <- swereg::tteplan_osf_text(
  "/path/to/spec/spec_v001.yaml",
  code_registry = study,
  global_max_isoyearweek = "2025-01",
  people = c("woman", "women")
)
cat(osf[["Data inclusion and exclusion"]])
```

The text prints the `name` of each criterion, covariate and outcome, the `description` of each outcome and treatment, and the arm labels, as the specification writes them. Write those fields for a reader of the registration: no variable names, no internal version or approach numbers. The categories of a covariate are data values, so they appear in the code list only. The author writes the fields that the specification cannot answer: the title, the research question and the primary result, the foreknowledge, the data sources and the ethics approval.

Build the registration document from these texts, for example in a `.qmd` that calls the function. Do not copy the text by hand: a copy goes stale when the specification changes.

# The OSF sections, field by field

The YAML column names a key of the specification. `vignette("tte-spec-schema")`
lists every legal key. The Excel column names a section of the Study
Specification sheet, and a row label where one applies. TARGET items come from
`$print_target_checklist()` on the same plan.

| OSF section | YAML key | Excel specification |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Research questions or hypotheses | `study$description`, `outcomes[]`, `enrollments[]$treatment$arms` | Outcomes; Enrollments, rows "Treatment:" and "Comparator:" |
| Foreknowledge of data or evidence | n/a | n/a. See "Foreknowledge". |
| Study type | Non-randomized study. Adjustment or control-based design: the treatment and censoring weights. | n/a |
| Intention for causal interpretation | The estimands of TARGET item 6f | n/a |
| Blinding of experimental treatments | No blinding is involved. | n/a |
| Additional blinding during research or analysis | n/a | n/a. See "Foreknowledge". |
| Study design | `target_trial`, `enrollments[]`, `follow_up[]` | Study, row "Design:"; Follow-up; Enrollments; the Target trial protocol sheet. TARGET items 6a to 6h and 7. |
| Randomization | Not applicable. The comparator draw is seeded sampling, with `enrollments[]$treatment$implementation$seed`. | n/a |
| Data collection procedures | `inclusion_criteria`, `exclusion_criteria`, `enrollments[]$additional_inclusion`, `enrollments[]$additional_exclusion`, `enrollments[]$observed_var` | Inclusion criteria (global); Exclusion criteria (global); Enrollments, rows "Additional inclusion:" and "Additional exclusion:" |
| Sample size | n/a | n/a. See "Sample size". |
| Sample size rationale | `enrollments[]$treatment$implementation$comparator_to_intervention_ratio` | Enrollments, row "Comparator-to-intervention ratio:". See "Sample size". |
| Starting and stopping rules | `inclusion_criteria$isoyears`, `follow_up[]$weeks`, the `global_max_isoyearweek` argument of s0 | Inclusion criteria (global), row "Isoyears:"; Follow-up; Study, row "Admin censoring:" |
| Manipulated variables | None | n/a |
| Measured variables | `enrollments[]$treatment`, `outcomes[]`, `confounders[]`, the criteria, `subgroups[]` | Enrollments; Outcomes; Confounders; the criteria sections. The sheet does not list `subgroups[]`. |
| Indices | `confounders[]` with `implementation$computed: true`, and their `source_variable` and `window` | Confounders, rows "Variable:" and "Window:" |
| Statistical models | Fixed by swereg | `vignette("tte-methods")`, section 1. TARGET item 6h. |
| Transformations | n/a | See "Transformations". |
| Inference criteria | `study$implementation$conf_level`, default 0.95, and `min_expected_events_per_arm_per_year` | `vignette("tte-methods")`, section 1.8.6. `tteplan_osf_text()` writes the minimum-events rule as the `Inference criteria` field. |
| Data inclusion and exclusion | The criteria of "Data collection procedures", and `rare_condition_rule` | Confounders, rows of "Rare-condition rule (rare_condition_rule)". TARGET items 6a and 7. See "The rare-condition rule". |
| Missing data | Fixed rules, and the `impute_fn` argument of s1 | `vignette("tte-methods")`, section 1.8.7. TARGET item 11. |
| Other planned analyses | `subgroups[]`, the untruncated weights, and the intention-to-treat estimand beside the per-protocol one | `vignette("tte-methods")`, sections 1.8.8 and 1.9 |
| Context and additional information | `study$implementation$version` | Study, row "Version:". See "Deviations after registration". |

## Statistical models

Section 1 of `vignette("tte-methods")` states the estimators as swereg
implements them. Copy it without change, so the protocol matches the code. Then
state each value of its list "Values your protocol must state".

## Transformations

swereg does not transform a confounder. The treatment weight model and the
censoring models hold each confounder as one main-effect term, with no
interaction and no spline. A numeric column enters as one linear term. A
logical column enters as one term for `TRUE`. A character or factor column
enters through the default treatment coding of R, so its first level is the
reference.

Derive any other coding in the skeleton, and register the derived column.
Section 1.8.9 of `vignette("tte-methods")` states the time terms of the outcome
and censoring models.

## Inference criteria

The intervals of the rate ratio and of the risk difference use
`study$implementation$conf_level`. Standard errors are clustered on the
person. swereg applies no correction for multiple outcomes or multiple
comparisons. State your own rule in the form.

# The rare-condition rule

A `rare_condition_rule` block in the specification is a pre-specified rule. Each
candidate confounder held by fewer than `min_n` persons in the smallest arm of
the driving comparisons becomes an exclusion criterion of every comparison.
The other candidates stay confounders. Each candidate is the variable of a
confounder with `computed: true`.

```yaml
confounders:
  - name: "Prior ischaemic stroke"
    implementation:
      source_variable: osd_i63
      window: lifetime_before_baseline
      computed: true

rare_condition_rule:
  min_n: 100
  decided_by: ["01"]
  candidates: [rd_no_osd_i63_everbefore]
```

`decided_by` names the driving comparisons. The rule is decided from baseline
counts in the eligible population, before the comparator draw and without
follow-up outcomes. s1 makes that decision.

At registration, nobody knows which conditions the rule excludes. Register the
threshold, the driving comparisons and the candidates. The Excel specification
states the rule and the row "Decision:" reads "not decided yet (s1 has not run)".
TARGET item 6a gives the same rule as prose. Paste it into "Data inclusion and
exclusion".

# Sample size

At registration there are no study counts. Base the rationale on external
information, such as a published incidence, or an earlier extraction that you
document as such.

The minimum detectable effect (MDE) columns of the `$export_tables()` workbook
are not a preregistration input. swereg computes them after s3, from the
study's own events.

To plan from external numbers, apply the naive Poisson formula that the MDE
columns use. Under the null, both arms share one rate. In the workbook, that
rate is the pooled weighted rate of both arms. At registration, it is the
external rate:

```{r}
mde <- function(rate, py_int, py_cmp, power = 0.8, conf_level = 0.95) {
  e_int <- rate * py_int
  e_cmp <- rate * py_cmp
  se <- sqrt(1 / e_int + 1 / e_cmp)
  k <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf_level) / 2) + qnorm(power)
  round(c(
    intervention_events = e_int,
    comparator_events = e_cmp,
    mde_protective = exp(-k * se),
    mde_harmful = exp(k * se)
  ), 2)
}

# External rate: 4 events per 1,000 person-years in both arms.
# 3,000 intervention person-trials and 6,000 comparator person-trials,
# with a 5-year horizon.
mde(rate = 4 / 1000, py_int = 3000 * 5, py_cmp = 6000 * 5)
```

The person-years in this example are the person-trials times the horizon. That
is an upper bound, because loss, death and the end of data stop follow-up
early. The formula ignores the repeated contributions of one person to many
trials. So it can differ from the detectable effect of the weighted estimator
with person-clustered standard errors.

The minimum-events rule computes the same expected events under the null for
each follow-up year of 52 weeks. The expected events of an arm are the pooled
weighted rate of both arms times the weighted person-years of the arm. When an
arm falls below `min_expected_events_per_arm_per_year` in one year, s3
withholds the rate ratio, the risk difference and the number needed to treat
of that estimand. Check each arm and year against the threshold, which is 5
in this example:

```{r}
# Expected events per arm and follow-up year. Each person-trial contributes
# at most 1 person-year per year, so these values are an upper bound.
expected_per_year <- (4 / 1000) * c(intervention = 3000, comparator = 6000)
expected_per_year
expected_per_year >= 5
```

At s3, the pooled rate holds the observed events of both arms. So the years
that pass depend on the outcome data. The rule is a prespecified reporting
rule. The rule decides the per-protocol estimand, and the intention-to-treat
estimand follows that decision. The `Minimum events (Y or -)` sheet of the
workbook shows the verdict of the rule. The `Minimum events (#)` sheet shows
the largest cut at which each estimate still passes the rule.

# Foreknowledge

At registration the authors ran s0 only, and s0 reads no outcome value. State
that under "Explanation of foreknowledge".

After registration, s1 reads outcome data. A person enters a trial only if they
reach time zero free of every outcome of the enrollment. So every s1 count from
the attrition step "Event before time zero" onwards depends on outcome events
before time zero. The s1 panel files, `file_raw` and `file_imp`, also hold the
follow-up outcomes. Do not open those files before the analysis. If an author
sees an outcome-dependent result before the analysis, record it in the
deviations log.

# Deviations after registration

After registration, a change to the specification is a new specification
version, with a new Excel specification:

1. Copy the registered `spec_vNNN.yaml` to the next version number.
2. Make the change, and set `study$implementation$version` and `date`.
3. Build the plan from s0, and write the new Excel specification with
   `$excel_spec_summary()`.
4. Write one log entry: the date, the change and the reason.

Each version writes to its own results directory, because `plan$dir_results`
appends the version. s0 stops when `study$implementation$version` differs from
its `spec_version` argument. Do not edit the registered version. Compare two
versions with `git diff --no-index` on their YAML files. Report the log with
the paper.
